stem: Match each CSDM domain to what it primarily organizes?

pairs.right: Core reference data: companies, locations, users, groups
Business and application services as a service blueprint
Technical services and the CIs that support them
Service offerings consumed through the catalog and portfolio

rationale: CSDM groups CMDB data into domains: Foundation holds core reference data; Design captures business/application services; Manage Technical Services covers technical services and supporting CIs; Sell/Consume represents service offerings consumed via the catalog.

stem: Match each CMDB concept to the table that stores it?

pairs.right: cmdb_ci
cmdb_rel_ci
cmdb_ci_business_app
service_offering

rationale: Base CIs live in cmdb_ci; relationships in cmdb_rel_ci; business applications in cmdb_ci_business_app; commercial commitments in service_offering.

stem: Match each service-model term to its definition?

pairs.right: A service the business consumes to achieve an outcome
An internal service that supports business services
A running instance of an application and its supporting CIs
A specific level or commitment at which a service is offered

rationale: The CSDM service model distinguishes business services (consumed for outcomes), technical services (internal support), application services (running app plus CIs), and service offerings (committed levels of a service).

stem: Match each CSDM domain to a representative activity?

pairs.right: Maintain accurate companies, locations, users, and groups
Define business applications and the service portfolio
Map technical services to the CIs that support them
Use the model to drive events, incidents, and changes

rationale: Each CSDM domain anchors typical work: Foundation maintains reference data; Design defines services; Manage Technical Services maps supporting CIs; Operate uses the model operationally.

stem: Match each CSDM domain to an example record?

pairs.right: A location record for the London office
The 'Customer Portal' business application
An application service supporting the portal
An incident raised against a service CI

rationale: Concrete examples clarify the domains: a location is Foundation data; a business application is Design; an application service is Manage Technical Services; an operational incident is Operate.

stem: Match each CMDB Health KPI to what it measures?

pairs.right: Required attributes and relationships are populated
CI data is accurate, including duplicates and stale records
CIs follow recommended CSDM classes and relationships
CIs not updated within an expected period

rationale: CMDB Health scores completeness (populated data), correctness (accuracy/duplicates/staleness), and compliance (CSDM conformance); staleness is a correctness signal for data not refreshed in time.

stem: Match each IRE component to its function?

pairs.right: Decides whether an incoming CI already exists
Controls which source may update an attribute
Ranks authoritative sources when they conflict
Attributes and criteria used to match a CI uniquely

rationale: The Identification and Reconciliation Engine uses identification rules to match incoming CIs, reconciliation rules and datasource precedence to control which source wins an attribute, and identifiers to define matching criteria.

stem: Match each data-certification element to its role?

pairs.right: A scheduled review confirming CI data is accurate
Defines which records a certification covers
A work item to verify a set of records
Triggers follow-on remediation

rationale: Data Certification schedules attestation of CI accuracy: a filter scopes the records, tasks are generated for review, and failures drive remediation.

stem: Match each governance role to its responsibility?

pairs.right: Owns CMDB data quality and governance
Accountable for a specific CI's accuracy
Owns standards for a CI class
Accountable for a service's data

rationale: Governance assigns clear ownership: the Data Manager owns overall quality, CI owners their CIs, class owners their class standards, and service owners their service data.

stem: Match each deduplication concept to its meaning?

pairs.right: Two CIs representing the same real item
A work item to merge or remediate duplicates
Prevents duplicates during ingestion
Keeps a single authoritative value per attribute

rationale: Duplicates are multiple records for one item; de-duplication tasks remediate them, while identification rules prevent them at ingestion and reconciliation keeps one authoritative value.

stem: Match each CMDB health issue to an example?

pairs.right: A server CI missing its owned-by relationship
Two CIs for the same physical server
An application service missing required relationships
A CI last scanned nine months ago

rationale: Examples ground the health metrics: missing relationships are incompleteness; duplicates are incorrectness; missing CSDM relationships are non-compliance; un-refreshed CIs are stale.

stem: Match each governance concept to its definition?

pairs.right: Policies and ownership ensuring trustworthy CI data
Periodic attestation that data is correct
Tracking of changes to CI records over time
Correcting data-quality issues that are found

rationale: Governance combines policy/ownership, certification (attestation), auditing (change tracking), and remediation (fixing issues) to keep the CMDB trustworthy.

stem: Match each CMDB Health dashboard element to its meaning?

pairs.right: A visual summary of CMDB health scores
Health score for a specific CI class
A measured indicator such as completeness
A list of CIs failing a specific metric

rationale: The health dashboard summarizes scores; scorecards break them down by class; KPIs are the measured indicators; drilldowns list the failing CIs.

stem: Match each IRE identification term to its meaning?

pairs.right: A CI identified on its own attributes
A CI identified relative to its parent, such as a disk on a server
Matches related or contained CIs
Priority-ordered criteria within an identifier

rationale: IRE identifies independent CIs by their own attributes and dependent CIs relative to a parent; lookup-based entries match contained CIs, and identifier entries are tried in priority order.

stem: Match each data-quality dimension to the question it answers?

pairs.right: Are required fields filled in?
Is the data accurate and unique?
Does the CI follow CSDM standards?
Is the data up to date?

rationale: Each quality dimension answers a question: completeness (fields filled), correctness (accurate/unique), compliance (CSDM-conformant), and timeliness (current).

stem: Match each remediation approach to how it is handled?

pairs.right: A flow or rule fixes the issue without a person
Routed to the responsible owner to fix
Governance owner triages systemic issues
Legitimately omits records from a metric

rationale: Remediation can be automated, assigned to an owner, escalated to the Data Manager for systemic issues, or formally excepted when omission is justified.

stem: Match each governance tool or artifact to its purpose?

pairs.right: Admin console for managing CMDB health and data
Tracks completeness, correctness, and compliance
Confirms data accuracy on a schedule
Defines ownership and standards

rationale: CMDB Workspace is the management console; the health dashboard tracks scores; certification confirms accuracy on schedule; governance policy defines ownership and standards.

stem: Match each multisource term to its role?

pairs.right: Tracks attribute values per data source
Determines the winning value across sources
Restricts which source can write an attribute
Identifies where a CI's data originated

rationale: Multisource CMDB stores per-source values; precedence picks the winner; reconciliation rules restrict who can write; the discovery source records data origin.

stem: Match each data-certification lifecycle step to its action?

pairs.right: Create the certification filter and schedule
The system creates certification tasks
The owner confirms or corrects records
Fix records that fail the review

rationale: Certification flows define (filter/schedule), generate (tasks), review (confirm/correct), and remediate (fix failures).

stem: Match each governance goal to the behavior it drives?

pairs.right: Relationships and required fields are populated
Few duplicates and little stale data
CIs adhere to CSDM
Every CI and class has an accountable owner

rationale: Governance goals translate to behaviors: completeness (populated data), correctness (low duplicates/staleness), compliance (CSDM adherence), and ownership (accountable owners).

stem: Match each CI data-quality term to its definition?

pairs.right: Install-status values from planned to retired
A CI not updated within an expected window
A CI with no relationships
Multiple records for one real item

rationale: Common quality terms: lifecycle (install status), stale (not refreshed), orphan (no relationships), and duplicate (multiple records for one item).

stem: Match each CMDB relationship to its meaning?

pairs.right: One CI relies on another to function
Software runs on a host CI
A CI is part of a parent CI
A CI is hosted by infrastructure

rationale: Relationship types are directional pairs: Depends on/Used by (reliance), Runs on/Runs (software on host), Contains/Contained by (composition), Hosted on/Hosts (hosting).

stem: Match each Insight tool to its use?

pairs.right: Visually query CIs and their relationships
Monitor completeness, correctness, and compliance
Visualize a CI and its related CIs
Summarize CMDB data in charts and lists

rationale: Query Builder builds relationship queries; the health dashboard monitors data quality; the dependency/BSM map visualizes a CI's neighborhood; reports summarize data.

stem: Match each CMDB group concept to its meaning?

pairs.right: A reusable set of CIs
CIs added explicitly to the group
Membership derived from a filter
Scope health, certification, or remediation

rationale: CMDB groups are reusable CI sets; membership can be manual or filter-driven (dynamic), and groups scope health, certification, and remediation.

stem: Match each relationship reading to its meaning?

pairs.right: A needs B
B is consumed by A
The 'Contains' side of a relationship
The 'Contained by' side of a relationship

rationale: Reading relationships: Depends on means needs; Used by is the reverse; the Contains side is the parent and Contained by is the child.

stem: Match each deduplication step to its action?

pairs.right: Find candidate duplicate CIs
Confirm which CIs are truly duplicates
Pick the master record to keep
Combine or remove the duplicates

rationale: Deduplication detects candidates, reviews them, chooses a surviving master, then merges or removes the rest.

stem: Match each Query Builder element to its role?

pairs.right: Restricts which CIs are returned
Traverses from one CI to related CIs
Limits the query to a CI class
The CIs matching the query

rationale: Query Builder uses filter conditions to restrict CIs, relationship hops to traverse links, class scope to target a class, and returns a result list.

stem: Match each CMDB health score to what it reflects?

pairs.right: How fully CIs are populated
How accurate and unique CIs are
How well CIs follow CSDM
How a score changes over time

rationale: Health scores reflect completeness (populated), correctness (accurate/unique), and compliance (CSDM), and trends show change over time.

stem: Match each CMDB group scoping use to its purpose?

pairs.right: Run health metrics against a CI group
Certify the CIs in a group
Target remediation to a group
Report on a group's CIs

rationale: Groups scope work: health metrics, certification, remediation, and reporting can each be targeted at a defined CI group.

stem: Match each Insight capability to its description?

pairs.right: Graphical map of a CI and related CIs
Build multi-class relationship queries
Scores for CMDB data quality
Reusable saved set of CIs

rationale: Insight capabilities: dependency views map relationships, Query Builder builds relationship queries, the health dashboard scores quality, and groups save reusable CI sets.

stem: Match each ingestion method to its use?

pairs.right: Agentless scanning of infrastructure via a MID Server
Builds application services and their dependencies
Integration that loads third-party CI data
Directly creating CI records

rationale: CIs enter the CMDB via Discovery (scanning), Service Mapping (application services), Service Graph Connectors (third-party data), or manual entry.

stem: Match each Discovery phase to its action?

pairs.right: Probes detect active devices
Determine the device or CI type
Match to an existing CI or create one
Gather detailed attributes and relationships

rationale: Discovery runs in four phases: scanning (detect), classification (type), identification (match/create), and exploration (detailed attributes and relationships).

stem: Match each import pipeline component to its role?

pairs.right: Defines where import data comes from
Staging area for incoming rows
Maps staging fields to the target table
Matches rows to update versus insert

rationale: The import pipeline uses a data source (origin), an import set table (staging), a transform map (field mapping), and coalesce fields (match for update vs insert).

stem: Match each Discovery component to its job?

pairs.right: Executes Discovery and integrations on the local network
Collects data from a target
Processes probe results into CIs
Authenticates the MID Server to targets

rationale: Discovery relies on the MID Server (executes on-network), probes (collect), sensors (process into CIs), and credentials (authenticate to targets).

stem: Match each IRE ingestion step to its purpose?

pairs.right: Find a matching CI for incoming data
Create a CI when no match exists
Apply attributes per reconciliation rules
Decide which source's value wins

rationale: When data is ingested through IRE, it identifies a match, inserts when none exists, updates per reconciliation rules, and reconciles conflicting source values.

stem: Match each IntegrationHub ETL step to its action?

pairs.right: Read records from the source payload
Map and convert to CMDB structure
Insert or update CIs through identification
Configure source-to-CMDB field maps

rationale: IntegrationHub ETL extracts source records, transforms them to CMDB structure, loads through IRE, using configured field mappings.

stem: Match each Service Graph Connector concept to its meaning?

pairs.right: A prebuilt integration to load CI data
The external system providing data
Ensures imported CIs are identified and reconciled
Aligns source fields to CMDB classes

rationale: Service Graph Connectors are prebuilt integrations: a source system provides data, IRE identifies/reconciles it, and mapping aligns fields to CMDB classes.

stem: Match each data source type to how it loads data?

pairs.right: Pulls rows from an external database
Loads records from a file
Receives data from a web service
Populates CIs by scanning infrastructure

rationale: Data sources vary: JDBC pulls from databases, file sources load CSV/Excel, REST/API receives web-service data, and Discovery scans infrastructure.

stem: Match each CMDB table to its purpose?

pairs.right: Base table for all configuration items
Stores relationships between CIs
Service CIs
Business application CIs

rationale: Key CMDB tables: cmdb_ci (base CIs), cmdb_rel_ci (relationships), cmdb_ci_service (services), and cmdb_ci_business_app (business applications).

stem: Match each CI Class Manager capability to its function?

pairs.right: View parent and child CI classes
Define fields on a class
Configure how CIs in a class are matched
Define allowed relationships for a class

rationale: CI Class Manager manages the class hierarchy, attributes, identification rules, and relationship rules for CI classes from one place.

stem: Match each reclassification action to its meaning?

pairs.right: Move a CI to a more specific child class
Move a CI to a parent or less specific class
Move a CI to a class in a different branch
Changing a CI's class

rationale: Reclassification changes a CI's class: upgrade (more specific), downgrade (less specific), or switch (different branch of the hierarchy).

stem: Match each CMDB structure term to its definition?

pairs.right: A type or table of CI, such as Linux Server
A field on a CI, such as serial number
A typed link between two CIs
A single CI record

rationale: CMDB structure: a class is a CI type/table, an attribute is a field, a relationship is a typed link, and a CI is one record.

stem: Match each class to its place in the CMDB hierarchy?

pairs.right: Root class that all CIs extend
Hardware CIs
Computer CIs that extend hardware
Server CIs that extend computer

rationale: The CMDB class hierarchy descends from cmdb_ci to cmdb_ci_hardware to cmdb_ci_computer to cmdb_ci_server, each extending the one above.

stem: Match each multisource attribute mechanism to its role?

pairs.right: Stores per-source attribute values
Limits which source updates an attribute
Selects the winning value
Shows which source last changed a value

rationale: Multisource CMDB stores values per source; reconciliation rules limit writers; precedence selects the winner; audit shows the last source to change a value.

stem: Match each class-governance element to its role?

pairs.right: Accountable for a CI class's standards
Oversees overall CMDB data quality
Tool to configure classes and rules
Defines how CIs in a class are matched

rationale: Class governance assigns a class owner for standards, a Data Manager for overall quality, uses CI Class Manager to configure classes, and identification rules to match CIs.
